 Deepchand Sahu

 The State Of Madhya Pradesh

 Order

This criminal appeal has been filed under Section 14-A of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,
1989.

2 . Appellant is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.315 of 2025 registered at Police Station- Shahpura, District- Dindori for the offences punishable under Sections 74, 75(1)(ii),
296, 115(2) and 351(3) of BNS and Sections 3 (1)(da), 3(1)(Gha), 3(1)(w)(i) and 3(2)(va) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
3.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is an practicing Advocate and respondent/complainant is Sarpanch.
It is also urged that on 08.05.2025, prosecutrix assaulted and beat appellant in the middle of the market.
Thereafter, prosecutrix lodged FIR against appellant with respect NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:30301 2 CRA-5387-2025 to molestation.
It is also urged that with respect to aforesaid, present appellant also lodged report against complainant.
It is also urged that prior to 08.05.2025, prosecutrix has also lodged an FIR against appellant for offence under Section 376 of the IPC on 15.01.2023, crime number thereof is 19/2023.

It is also urged that prosecutrix's son is supplier of Sand/stone and prior to 15.01.2023, prosecutrix's son had supplied sand/stone to Gram Panchayat of Amera of the amount of Rs.21,00,000/- in the Deepchand Sahu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116021015/
1 year 2021-2022.

sentences.text: Bills thereof are still pending.

3 . It is also urged on behalf of appellant that five criminal cases are pending against prosecutrix and her husband and prosecutrix engaged appellant as her counsel to contest on her behalf in aforesaid cases.
It is also urged that during aforesaid pendency of criminal cases, prosecutrix started treating appellant as brother.
Thereafter, prosecutrix demanded some money from appellant for marriage of her son.
Thereafter, appellant gave prosecutrix Rs.2,00,000/- on 01.07.2021.

Thereafter,
prosecutrix again demanded money when a child was born to her son.
Thereafter, on 16.06.2022 also, appellant gave cheque of Rs.75,000/- to prosecutrix.

When appellant demanded back aforesaid money, then, prosecutrix threatened appellant on WhatsApp continuously and thereafter, lodged FIR under Section 376 of the IPC (Crime No.19 of 2023) against appellant.
4 . Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the instant case.
Victim earlier lodged a false FIR against the appellant, in which she alleged that the appellant committed rape against her.

The appellant was granted bail by this NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:30301 3 CRA-5387-2025 Court, and the said FIR has been challenged before this Court vide M.Cr.C. No.25503/24, in which further proceedings before the Special Court, Dindori, are stayed.
Complainant is habitual in lodging false and fabricated complaints against anyone whenever any enmity arises.
5 . Further, it is contended that present appellant is an Advocate and filed a contempt case before the police authority, where the police failed to comply with the order passed by this Court.
Therefore, the police have supported the victim in lodging the false complaint against the appellant on the basis of her ST caste.
Victim is also a habitual offender; she has registered a number of cases in the Police Station Shahpura, and the police have supported her and have not arrested her.

6 . Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that the victim committed assault (marpeet)
on the appellant in front of a liquor shop on Umaria Road.
The incident, which took place on that day, was captured on video by the public and media, which clearly shows that the victim assaulted the appellant by slapping him and also using her chappal.

Therefore, police of Police Station - Shahpura have also registered an offence against the victim under Sections 115(2), 296, 351 and (3)(v) of BNS in connection with Crime No. 316/25 on the same day and time and allegation regarding the incident near the Tehsil is totally false and fabricated.
Appellant has neither met the victim near Tehsil Shahpura nor committed any such offence there; the offence took place only in front of the liquor shop on Umaria Road, Shahpura.
The victim made the complaint against the appellant to cover up her own act of assaulting him.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:30301 4 CRA-5387-2025 7.

Learned counsel for the appellant also submits that victim has made various complaints against the appellant because she is a Sarpanch in Gram Panchayat Amera and has embezzled public money of the Gram Panchayat.
The public of the Gram Panchayat filed a complaint under Section 40 of the M.P. Panchayat Rajya Gram Swaraj Adhiniyam before the SDM, in which proceedings have been initiated.

The appellant has also filed a writ petition before this Court for conducting an enquiry and Deepchand Sahu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116021015/
2 lodging an FIR against the victim, which has been registered.

sentences.text: The victim has been granted anticipatory bail by this Court on the condition that she deposits 50% of the embezzled money.
Due to this enmity with the appellant, the victim made a false and fabricated report against the appellant.
With regard to the incident near Tehsil Shahpura, no MLC was conducted by any doctor as alleged in the FIR.
There are more than 10 criminal cases registered against the victim at Police Station Shahpura.
She is a habitual offender and habitually makes false and fabricated reports against persons with whom she has enmity.
Police party is intentionally torturing and harassing the appellant and his family members.
Appellant has not committed any offence, and the allegations of the complainant are bogus and concocted.
8. Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that again prosecutrix filed FIR against appellant on 04.07.2023 for offence under Section 279 of the IPC (Crime No. 623 of 2023).
In this case, police has filed "Khatama report" on 29.12.2023.
It is also urged that prosecutrix and other persons entered into the house and assaulted appellant's son.

With respect to aforesaid, a complaint was filed on 25.09.2024 against prosecutrix, SDOP, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:30301 5 CRA-5387-2025 TI and S.P Dindori.

On account of aforesaid dispute,
present FIR pertaining to outrage of modesty has been lodged.
It is also urged that Investigating Officer is conducting the Investigation in a biased manner.
Offence is not punishable for more than seven years.
Therefore, principle laid down in Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar (2014) 8 SCC 273 is applicable to the facts and circumstances of the case.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar (2014) 8 SCC 273
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also urged that pertaining to criminal antecedents of appellant, prior to the year 2008, appellant's name has been deleted from "Gunda register" vide order dated 04.10.2017.

It is also urged that while passing judgment on 21.09.2021,
Sessions Court has commented that prosecutrix is habitual of making complaints.

In aforesaid case,
which pertains to Section 354 of the IPC, Sessions Court has acquitted appellant.
It is also urged that prima-facie , no case under SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act is made out.

With respect to above,
learned counsel for the appellant has relied upon in the case of Criminal Appeal No.11883 of 2022 (Aaditya Dev Parmar Vs. The State of M.P. and others) order dated 10.01.2023.

entities.text: Criminal Appeal No.11883 of 2022 (Aaditya Dev Parmar Vs. The State of M.P. and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On above grounds, it is urged that the appellant be granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.
9. Learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State as well as learned counsel for the objector/complainant submits that prima-facie, offence under SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act is made out.
Therefore, in view of Section 18 of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, appellant's application for anticipatory bail is not maintainable.

Further, in view of allegations levelled in FIR,
appellant is not entitled to be released on anticipatory bail.

10. This court has examined submissions of learned counsel for the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:30301 6 CRA-5387-2025 parties and perused record of the case/case diary in the light of submissions of both the parties.
1 1 . Admittedly, appellant is a practicing Advocate.

Present case pertains to Crime No.315 of 2025 for offence under Sections 74, 75(i)(ii), 296, 115(2), 351(3) of BNS and Sections 3(1)(r), 3(1)(s),
3(i)(W)(i) and 3(2) (va) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
Aforesaid incident is said to have occurred on 08.05.2025 at about 17:30 to 18:30 in front of Tahsil and near liquor shop Umaria road.

3 12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Crime No.316 of 2025 pertains to Sections 296, 115(2), 351(3) and 3(5) of BNS and this report has been lodged by appellant against prosecutrix, her husband and others persons for offence that was allegedly committed on 08.05.2025 at about 18:15 to 18:30 near Kirana shop by the side of liquor shop, Umaria road, Shahpura.

13. On 14.01.2023 also, prosecutrix lodged FIR against present appellant for offence under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), 294 and 506 of the IPC and Sections 3(1)(w)(ii) and 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
As per (Annexure P/1), aforesaid offence was allegedly committed from 10.12.2017 to 18.05.2022 and crime number of aforesaid is 19/2023.
14. Annexure P/3 reveals that on 04.07.2023, prosecutrix lodged report against present appellant for offence under Section 279 of the IPC and crime number of aforesaid is 623/2023.
As per Annexure P/4, after investigation, in aforeasid offence, police filed "Khatama report" as no offence was proved against the appellant with respect to aforesaid crime number.
15. Annexure P/9

reveals that prosecutrix had lodged FIR against one NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:30301 7 CRA-5387-2025 Jailal for offence under Sections 294, 354, 354(a)(1)(ii),
451 and 506 of the IPC.
Crime number of aforesaid is 470/2015 and incident is of 17.07.2015.

Aforesaid case was registered as RCT No.384 of 2015 and in aforesaid case, appellant Jailal was acquitted by Sessions Court vide judgment dated 21.09.2021 passed in Cr,A.No.02/2021.
16.

Hence, having regard to facts mentioned in the preceding paras and having regard to level of rivalry/animosity between the parties as well as incident as narrated/mentioned in FIR of Crime No.315 of 2025 and time, and place of incident thereof, in this Court's considered opinion,
prima-facie , no case/offence under SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is made out.
17. Further, having regard to aforesaid, in this Court's considered opinion, appellant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail.
Consequently, this appeal stands allowed.

18. It is directed that in the event of his arrest, present appellant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs.15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer.

It is also directed that the applicant shall abide by the conditions as enumerated under Section 482 (2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
19.

It is made clear that appellant shall appear before the Investigating Officer as & when he is so directed and co-operate with the investigation and he shall also appear before the Trial Court, failing which his bail shall automatically stand cancelled without further reference to the Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:30301 8 CRA-5387-2025 20.
Accordingly, this appeal stands allowed and disposed of.
